# pubber-subber — full reference

> Transport-agnostic pub/sub for Node.js. One API across in-memory, Redis, Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, AWS SNS/SQS. Bring-your-own adapter for anything else. Optional RxJS bridge. TypeScript-first, dual ESM/CJS, zero-dependency core.

GitHub: https://github.com/samishal1998/pubber-subber

---

## 1. Concepts

- **`PubSub`** — the facade your app uses. Holds an adapter, tracks live subscription handles, merges default meta, dispatches errors to your `onError` callback.
- **Adapter** — implements `PubSubAdapter`. Maps the abstract `publish`/`subscribe` calls to a real transport (in-memory, Redis, Postgres, GCP, AWS, …).
- **`AdapterMessage<T>`** — what subscribers receive: `{ topic, payload, raw, meta, ack?, nack? }`.
- **Meta** — adapter-specific knobs passed as the last argument to every method. Three slots (`TPubMeta`, `TSubMeta`, `TUnsubMeta`) flow through types so you get IntelliSense for the chosen adapter.
- **`compose()`** — combines a publish-capable adapter and a subscribe-capable adapter into one (canonical use: AWS SNS + SQS).
- **Codec** — pluggable serializer (default JSON) used by adapters that need to encode payloads on the wire.

---

## 2. Install — adapter matrix

```sh
# Core (always required)
npm install @pubber-subber/core

# Pick one or more adapters
npm install @pubber-subber/memory                                  # in-process
npm install @pubber-subber/redis ioredis                            # Redis / Valkey / KeyDB / Dragonfly
npm install @pubber-subber/pg pg                                    # Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY
npm install @pubber-subber/gcp-pubsub @google-cloud/pubsub          # Google Cloud Pub/Sub
npm install @pubber-subber/aws-sns @aws-sdk/client-sns              # AWS SNS (publish-only)
npm install @pubber-subber/aws-sqs @aws-sdk/client-sqs              # AWS SQS (subscribe-only)
npm install @pubber-subber/rxjs rxjs                                # Optional RxJS bridge
```

Driver SDKs (`ioredis`, `pg`, `@google-cloud/pubsub`, `@aws-sdk/client-*`, `rxjs`) are **peer dependencies** — install only what you use.

Node 20.11+. ESM and CommonJS both supported.

---

## 3. Quick start

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { memory } from '@pubber-subber/memory';

const pubsub = new PubSub({ adapter: memory() });

const sub = await pubsub.subscribe('users.created', (msg) => {
  console.log(msg.topic, msg.payload);
});

await pubsub.publish('users.created', { id: 1, name: 'Alice' });

await sub.unsubscribe();
await pubsub.disconnect();
```

Swap `memory()` for `redis(...)`, `pg(...)`, `gcpPubSub(...)`, or a composed `awsSns()`/`awsSqs()` pair — nothing else in your code changes.

---

## 4. PubSub facade — full API

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';

const pubsub = new PubSub<TAdapter>({
  adapter: TAdapter,
  defaultMeta?: {
    publish?: PublishMetaOf<TAdapter>;
    subscribe?: SubscribeMetaOf<TAdapter>;
  };
  onError?: (
    err: unknown,
    ctx: { op: 'publish' | 'subscribe' | 'handler' | 'unsubscribe'; topic: string },
  ) => void;
});
```

### Methods

```ts
// Connect (lazy — auto-called on first op)
await pubsub.connect();

// Publish
await pubsub.publish<T>(
  topic: string,
  payload: T,
  meta?: PublishMetaOf<TAdapter>,
): Promise<void>;

// Subscribe — returns a SubscriptionHandle
const sub = await pubsub.subscribe<T>(
  topic: string,
  handler: (msg: AdapterMessage<T>, meta?: SubscribeMetaOf<TAdapter>) => void | Promise<void>,
  meta?: SubscribeMetaOf<TAdapter>,
): Promise<SubscriptionHandle>;

await sub.unsubscribe();
// sub.id, sub.topic also available

// Disconnect — unsubscribes all live handles, then closes the adapter
await pubsub.disconnect();

// State
pubsub.isConnected;         // boolean
pubsub.adapter;             // raw adapter, for escape hatches
```

### Meta merging

`defaultMeta.publish` (or `.subscribe`) is **merged** with the call-site meta on every call. Call-site keys win on collision. Merge is shallow (one level of object spread).

```ts
const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: redis({ url }),
  defaultMeta: { publish: { channel: 'fallback' } },
});

await pubsub.publish('t', payload);                          // sends to 'fallback'
await pubsub.publish('t', payload, { channel: 'override' }); // sends to 'override'
```

---

## 5. compose() — hybrid publisher + subscriber

For platforms that split publish from subscribe (canonical case: AWS, where SNS publishes and SQS receives):

```ts
import { PubSub, compose } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { awsSns } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sns';
import { awsSqs } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sqs';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: compose({
    publisher: awsSns({ region: 'us-east-1' }),
    subscriber: awsSqs({
      region: 'us-east-1',
      queueUrl: 'https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/000000000000/orders',
    }),
    name: 'sns-sqs', // optional
  }),
});
```

Capabilities are unioned (`publish` from publisher, `subscribe`/`patternSubscribe`/`ack` from subscriber). `connect`/`disconnect` fan out to both. `publish` routes to the publisher; `subscribe` routes to the subscriber.

---

## 6. Codecs

```ts
import { jsonCodec, passthroughCodec, type Codec } from '@pubber-subber/core';

interface Codec {
  readonly name: string;
  encode(value: unknown): string | Uint8Array;
  decode<T = unknown>(data: string | Uint8Array): T;
}
```

- **`jsonCodec()`** — default for adapters that don't override. `JSON.stringify` / `JSON.parse`, throwing `SerializationError` on failure.
- **`passthroughCodec()`** — for byte-pipe adapters; accepts only `string` or `Uint8Array`, throws otherwise.
- **Custom** — implement `Codec` for MessagePack, Protobuf, AVRO, etc.

```ts
import * as msgpack from '@msgpack/msgpack';

const msgpackCodec: Codec = {
  name: 'msgpack',
  encode: (v) => msgpack.encode(v),
  decode: (d) => msgpack.decode(d instanceof Uint8Array ? d : new TextEncoder().encode(d)),
};

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: redis({ url, codec: msgpackCodec }),
});
```

The memory adapter passes references and ignores `codec`; everything else accepts `opts.codec`.

---

## 7. Errors

All errors extend `PubSubError`, which extends `Error`.

```ts
import {
  PubSubError,
  NotSupportedError,
  ConnectionError,
  SerializationError,
  SubscriptionError,
  PublishError,
} from '@pubber-subber/core';

try {
  await pubsub.publish('t', payload);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof PublishError) { /* e.g. pg NOTIFY > 7500 bytes */ }
  if (err instanceof NotSupportedError) { /* op not supported */ }
  if (err instanceof PubSubError) { /* catches everything from this lib */ }
}
```

| Class | Thrown when |
| --- | --- |
| `NotSupportedError` | Adapter doesn't support the requested op (e.g. `subscribe()` on aws-sns). |
| `ConnectionError` | Connect or disconnect failed. |
| `SerializationError` | Codec encode/decode failed. |
| `SubscriptionError` | Subscribe wiring failed (e.g. missing config). |
| `PublishError` | Publish wiring failed (e.g. pg payload size limit). |

---

## 8. In-memory adapter — `@pubber-subber/memory`

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/memory
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { memory } from '@pubber-subber/memory';

const pubsub = new PubSub({ adapter: memory({ rawPayloads: false }) });

await pubsub.subscribe('users.*', (msg) => console.log(msg.topic, msg.payload));
await pubsub.publish('users.created', { id: 1 });
```

### Options

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rawPayloads` | `false` | If `true`, subscribers get the publisher's exact object reference. Default `structuredClone()`s payloads so subscribers can't mutate. |

### Capabilities

```
publish: true | subscribe: true | patternSubscribe: true | ack: false
```

### Pattern matching

- `*` matches within a segment (won't cross `.`)
- `**` matches across segments
- `?` matches one char (not `.`)

```ts
await pubsub.subscribe('users.*', handler);   // users.created — NOT users.created.email
await pubsub.subscribe('users.**', handler);  // users.created.email
```

---

## 9. Redis adapter — `@pubber-subber/redis`

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/redis ioredis
```

Works with Redis, Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly.

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { redis } from '@pubber-subber/redis';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: redis({ url: 'redis://localhost:6379' }),
});

await pubsub.subscribe('users.*', handler);   // auto -> PSUBSCRIBE
await pubsub.publish('users.created', { id: 1 });
```

### Options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | `redis://[:password@]host:port[/db]`, `rediss://` for TLS. |
| `options` | ioredis `RedisOptions`. Merged with `url`. |
| `clients` | `{ publisher: Redis; subscriber: Redis }` — bring your own. Adapter won't `quit()` them. Must be distinct clients. |
| `codec` | Default `jsonCodec()`. |

### Meta

- Publish: `{ channel?: string }` — override the wire channel without changing `AdapterMessage.topic`.
- Subscribe: `{ pattern?: boolean }` — force `PSUBSCRIBE` even without wildcards.

### Capabilities

```
publish: true | subscribe: true | patternSubscribe: true | ack: false
```

### Reconnect

ioredis handles socket reconnects. On `ready` the adapter re-subscribes all channels and patterns. Messages published while disconnected are lost (Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget).

### Local Redis

```sh
docker run --rm -d -p 6379:6379 redis:7
```

---

## 10. Postgres adapter — `@pubber-subber/pg`

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/pg pg
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { pg } from '@pubber-subber/pg';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: pg({ connectionString: 'postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db' }),
});

await pubsub.subscribe('outbox.processed', (msg) => console.log(msg.payload));
await pubsub.publish('outbox.processed', { outboxId: 42 });
```

### Options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `connectionString` | Standard libpq URL. |
| `config` | Full `pg.ClientConfig`. |
| `client` | Bring-your-own `pg.Client`. Adapter doesn't `connect()` / `end()` it. |
| `codec` | Default `jsonCodec()`. |

### Meta

- Publish: `{ channel?: string }`
- Subscribe: `{ channel?: string }`

### Capabilities

```
publish: true | subscribe: true | patternSubscribe: false | ack: false
```

### Postgres-specific constraints

- Channel names ≤ 63 bytes. Longer topics are hashed to `pubsub_<sha256[:32]>`; internal map preserves the original logical topic.
- NOTIFY payloads ≤ ~8000 bytes. Adapter rejects encoded payloads > 7500 bytes with `PublishError`. Pattern: publish a row id, resolve the body via `SELECT`.
- No wildcards. `capabilities.patternSubscribe = false`.
- One dedicated `pg.Client` per adapter for LISTEN traffic.
- Publishes use parameterized `SELECT pg_notify($1, $2)` — no SQL injection risk.

### Local Postgres

```sh
docker run --rm -d -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres postgres:16
```

---

## 11. Google Cloud Pub/Sub adapter — `@pubber-subber/gcp-pubsub`

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/gcp-pubsub @google-cloud/pubsub
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { gcpPubSub } from '@pubber-subber/gcp-pubsub';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: gcpPubSub({ projectId: 'my-project' }),
});

await pubsub.subscribe(
  'users.created',
  (msg) => console.log(msg.payload),
  { subscriptionName: 'workers-users-created' },
);

await pubsub.publish('users.created', { id: 1 }, {
  attributes: { tenantId: 't1' },
  orderingKey: 'user-1',
});
```

### Options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `projectId` | GCP project. Falls back to SDK auto-detection. |
| `client` | Pre-built `@google-cloud/pubsub` client. |
| `options` | Full `ClientConfig`. |
| `codec` | Default `jsonCodec()`. |
| `subscriptionPrefix` | Prefix for auto-generated subscription names (default `'pubber'`). |

### Meta

- Publish: `{ attributes?: Record<string, string>; orderingKey?: string }`
- Subscribe:
  - `subscriptionName: string` (required for production)
  - `createIfMissing?: boolean`
  - `subscriptionOptions?: CreateSubscriptionOptions`
  - `ephemeral?: boolean` (delete sub on unsubscribe — dev/test only)

### Capabilities

```
publish: true | subscribe: true | patternSubscribe: false | ack: true
```

### Ack semantics

- Resolve → `message.ack()`
- Throw → `message.nack()`
- Call `msg.ack()` / `msg.nack()` inside the handler for manual control; the adapter skips auto-resolve.

### Emulator for development

```sh
gcloud beta emulators pubsub start --project=test-project --host-port=0.0.0.0:8085
export PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST=localhost:8085
gcloud --project=test-project pubsub topics create demo-topic
```

---

## 12. AWS SNS adapter — `@pubber-subber/aws-sns` (publish-only)

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/aws-sns @aws-sdk/client-sns
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { awsSns } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sns';

const pubsub = new PubSub({ adapter: awsSns({ region: 'us-east-1' }) });
await pubsub.publish('arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:000:orders', { id: 1 });
```

### Options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `region` | AWS region. |
| `topicArn` | Default TopicArn for publishes. |
| `client` | Pre-built `SNSClient`. |
| `options` | Full `SNSClientConfig`. |
| `codec` | Default `jsonCodec()`. |

### Publish meta

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `topicArn` | Override per call. |
| `targetArn` | Mobile push endpoint. |
| `phoneNumber` | SMS recipient. |
| `messageAttributes` | Forwarded to SNS. |
| `messageGroupId`, `messageDeduplicationId` | FIFO topics. |
| `subject` | Email subject. |

### Capabilities

```
publish: true | subscribe: false | patternSubscribe: false | ack: false
```

`subscribe()` throws `NotSupportedError`. Pair with aws-sqs via `compose()` for full duplex.

### TopicArn resolution

1. The `topic` arg if it starts with `arn:aws:sns:`.
2. `opts.topicArn` otherwise.
3. `meta.topicArn` for per-call override.

---

## 13. AWS SQS adapter — `@pubber-subber/aws-sqs` (subscribe-only)

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/aws-sqs @aws-sdk/client-sqs
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { awsSqs } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sqs';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: awsSqs({
    region: 'us-east-1',
    queueUrl: 'https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/000:orders',
  }),
});

await pubsub.subscribe('orders', (msg) => process(msg.payload));
// auto-ack on resolve, auto-nack on throw
```

### Options

| Option | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `region` | AWS region. |
| `queueUrl` | Default queue URL. |
| `client` | Pre-built `SQSClient`. |
| `options` | Full `SQSClientConfig`. |
| `codec` | Default `jsonCodec()`. |

### Subscribe meta

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queueUrl` | `opts.queueUrl` | Required somewhere. |
| `waitTimeSeconds` | 20 | Long-poll wait. 0–20. |
| `maxMessages` | 10 | Per batch. 1–10. |
| `visibilityTimeout` | (queue default) | Per subscription. |
| `handlerConcurrency` | 5 | Max in-flight handlers. |

### Capabilities

```
publish: false | subscribe: true | patternSubscribe: false | ack: true
```

### Ack semantics

- Resolve → `DeleteMessage`.
- Throw → `ChangeMessageVisibility(VisibilityTimeout=0)` (immediate retry).
- Manual: `msg.ack()` / `msg.nack()` in handler.

### SNS → SQS envelope unwrapping

If the message body is an SNS notification envelope (`{"Type":"Notification","Message":"..."}`), the adapter unwraps it and decodes the inner `Message`. SNS attributes are exposed on `AdapterMessage.meta.snsAttributes`.

### LocalStack

```sh
docker run --rm -d -p 4566:4566 -e SERVICES=sns,sqs localstack/localstack
```

```ts
awsSqs({
  region: 'us-east-1',
  queueUrl: '...',
  options: { endpoint: 'http://localhost:4566' },
});
```

---

## 14. RxJS bridge — `@pubber-subber/rxjs`

```sh
npm install @pubber-subber/core @pubber-subber/rxjs rxjs
```

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { memory } from '@pubber-subber/memory';
import { fromTopic, toObservable } from '@pubber-subber/rxjs';
import { bufferTime, mergeMap, take, toArray } from 'rxjs';

const pubsub = new PubSub({ adapter: memory() });

// Unwrapped payload
fromTopic<{ id: number }>(pubsub, 'users.created')
  .subscribe((user) => console.log(user.id));

// Full envelope
toObservable<{ id: number }>(pubsub, 'users.*')
  .pipe(bufferTime(250), mergeMap((batch) => persist(batch)))
  .subscribe();
```

```ts
toObservable<T>(pubsub, topic, meta?): Observable<AdapterMessage<T>>
fromTopic<T>(pubsub, topic, meta?): Observable<T>
```

Both lazy-create the underlying pubsub subscription on first observer attach and tear it down on the last unsubscribe.

Teardown is safe even if it races with the initial `subscribe()` call.

---

## 15. Writing a custom adapter

```ts
import type {
  AdapterMessage,
  MessageHandler,
  PubSubAdapter,
  SubscriptionHandle,
} from '@pubber-subber/core';

interface MyPublishMeta { /* knobs on publish */ }
interface MySubscribeMeta { /* knobs on subscribe */ }

export function myAdapter(opts: MyOptions): PubSubAdapter<MyPublishMeta, MySubscribeMeta> {
  return {
    name: 'my-adapter',
    capabilities: {
      publish: true,
      subscribe: true,
      patternSubscribe: false,
      ack: false,
    },
    async connect() { /* ... */ },
    async disconnect() { /* ... */ },
    async publish(topic, payload, meta) { /* ... */ },
    async subscribe(topic, handler, meta): Promise<SubscriptionHandle> {
      // wire delivery, return a handle
      return { id: '...', topic, unsubscribe: async () => { /* ... */ } };
    },
  };
}
```

The three generic meta slots flow through the `PubSub` facade's types automatically via `PublishMetaOf<A>` / `SubscribeMetaOf<A>` — users get full IntelliSense for your knobs.

---

## 16. Conformance test kit

```ts
// my-adapter/test/conformance.test.ts
import { runConformance } from '@pubber-subber/core/testing';
import { myAdapter } from '../src/index.js';

runConformance({
  name: 'my-adapter',
  createAdapter: async () => myAdapter({ /* ... */ }),
  teardownAdapter: async (adapter) => { /* close conn / stop container */ },
  skip: {
    patternSubscribe: true,   // for adapters that can't support globs
    metadata: false,
    multipleSubscribers: false,
    lateSubscriber: false,
  },
  deliveryTimeoutMs: 5000,
  quietWindowMs: 500,
});
```

Tests covered: single round-trip, multi-subscriber fan-out, no replay for late subscribers, unsubscribe stops delivery, metadata pass-through, pattern subscriptions (when capability declared).

`vitest` is an optional peer dependency — only required when importing `@pubber-subber/core/testing`.

---

## 17. Common patterns

### Test/prod parity

Use the memory adapter in tests and a real one in prod — the rest of your code is unchanged:

```ts
import { PubSub, type PubSubAdapter } from '@pubber-subber/core';

function makePubSub(adapter: PubSubAdapter) {
  return new PubSub({ adapter });
}

// test
import { memory } from '@pubber-subber/memory';
const app = makePubSub(memory());

// prod
import { redis } from '@pubber-subber/redis';
const app = makePubSub(redis({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL! }));
```

### Typed payloads

```ts
interface UserCreated { id: number; name: string }

await pubsub.publish<UserCreated>('users.created', { id: 1, name: 'A' });

await pubsub.subscribe<UserCreated>('users.created', (msg) => {
  msg.payload.id;     // typed
});
```

### Tenant-scoped tracing via metadata

```ts
import { PubSub } from '@pubber-subber/core';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: ...,
  defaultMeta: { publish: { tenantId: getTenantId() } },
  onError: (err, ctx) => logger.error({ ...ctx, err }, 'pubsub error'),
});
```

### Manual ack / DLQ routing (GCP, SQS)

```ts
await pubsub.subscribe('payments', async (msg) => {
  try {
    await process(msg.payload);
    await msg.ack?.();
  } catch (err) {
    if (isTransient(err)) {
      await msg.nack?.();              // retry
    } else {
      await routeToDLQ(msg.payload, err);
      await msg.ack?.();               // don't retry — drop from queue
    }
  }
});
```

### Stream operations via RxJS

```ts
import { fromTopic } from '@pubber-subber/rxjs';
import { bufferTime, filter, mergeMap } from 'rxjs';

fromTopic<PageView>(pubsub, 'analytics.*')
  .pipe(
    filter((v) => !v.path.startsWith('/internal')),
    bufferTime(250),
    mergeMap((batch) => writeBatch(batch)),
  )
  .subscribe();
```

### SNS → SQS fan-out

```ts
import { PubSub, compose } from '@pubber-subber/core';
import { awsSns } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sns';
import { awsSqs } from '@pubber-subber/aws-sqs';

const pubsub = new PubSub({
  adapter: compose({
    publisher: awsSns({ region: 'us-east-1' }),
    subscriber: awsSqs({
      region: 'us-east-1',
      queueUrl: process.env.SQS_URL!,
    }),
  }),
});
```
